results.caption:
The house is falling apart, the electricity is on borrowed time, and six kids are raising themselves while their father drinks the disability checks, welcome to the Gallaghers. Shameless (2011) is Showtime's beloved chaos epic, the longest-running scripted series in the network's history, eleven seasons of South Side Chicago survival anchored by William H. Macy's magnificent trainwreck Frank and Emmy Rossum's fierce, exhausted Fiona.

The mood is poverty played with teeth and heart. The genius of the American adaptation, developed by John Wells from Paul Abbott's British original, is refusing pity: the Gallaghers scam, brawl, and hustle with jubilant creativity, squatting rights defended like castles, school lunches liberated, every utility bill a heist, while Macy's Frank delivers gutter philosophy monologues that somehow make a monstrous father mesmerizing television. Rossum's Fiona became the show's soul, a twenty-something surrendering her own life to keep five siblings fed, her arc of sacrifice, spirals, and hard-won selfhood ranking among television's great unsung performances. Around her, the kids grew into icons: Jeremy Allen White's brilliant, haunted Lip drinking away his potential, Cameron Monaghan's Ian and Noel Fisher's Mickey building Gallavich, the rough-edged love story fans championed into one of TV's most beloved queer romances, Emma Kenney's Debbie, Ethan Cutkosky's Carl, and neighbors Kev and V holding the block together. This is family storytelling without a safety net, comedy and tragedy drinking from the same bottle.

What makes it a must-see is the loyalty. The Gallaghers fail each other constantly and abandon each other never, and eleven seasons prove both halves of that sentence.

Save this post for your binge-worthy essentials collection, and share it with the sibling who would absolutely help you bury the evidence, no questions asked.

What Happened After South Korea’s World Cup Exit 🚨 The South Korea national team landed back home at 4 a.m. hoping to avoid the backlash after their World Cup exit, but hundreds of cameras were already waiting. Losing 1-0 to South Africa, a team ranked 23 places below them, caused a huge reaction across the country. Head coach Hong Myung-bo resigned right away, but the story didn’t end there. Hong was already a controversial hire after coaching South Korea at the 2014 World Cup, and people inside the federation later claimed the hiring process was handled badly. Even Park Ji-sung said the blame is on the people running South Korean football, not just the manager or players. Now the president has apologized to fans, pointed to the taxpayer money spent on the team, and ordered an investigation into what went wrong. #soccer #football #WorldCup #SouthKorea #FIFA

They're the most successful Asian nation in football history, qualifying for the most World Cups ever and finishing fourth at the 2002 World Cup which they hosted. But now they're under investigation by their own country's president. After benching Hyung-min's son in their World Cup exit against South Africa, who are ranked 25 spots lower than them in FIFA's rankings, it didn't matter if he resigned instantly. The whole country turned on their manager so bad, riot police were brought in and the team timed their arrival at 4 in the morning. The problem though is it isn't only his fault and that's why South Korea's president launched an investigation. You might not realize, but he already failed as their manager back in 2014, so when he was rehired two years ago, it was highly controversial. Members of the board in charge of hiring claimed the federation disregarded proper vetting procedures and that some members lacked professionalism and knowledge. That's why the president of the country posted this long message on X, acknowledging all the taxpayer money that's gone into the team and announcing the investigation to try to ensure this doesn't happen again. House (November 2004) is one of the greatest character driven medical dramas ever made and the show that completely reinvented Hugh Laurie's career, despite the fact that he almost did not get cast at all. Created by David Shore for Fox, the series follows Dr. Gregory House, an unconventional and brilliantly misanthropic diagnostician at the fictional Princeton-Plainsboro Teaching Hospital who relies as much on confrontation and instinct as medical training to solve the most baffling cases in medicine, while privately struggling with chronic pain and an addiction to Vicodin. [The Hollywood Reporter](https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/tv/tv-news/mika-abdalla-stephen-kalyn-dean-allie-off-campus-season-2-1236603976/) Laurie famously recorded his audition tape in a hotel bathroom in Namibia using an umbrella as a cane, with producer Bryan Singer so convinced he had found the perfect quintessentially American actor that he was stunned to learn Laurie was actually British. [justwatch](https://www.justwatch.com/sg/tv-show/off-campus)

The character was directly inspired by Sherlock Holmes, with House's drug dependence and brilliant, antisocial deduction skills mirroring Holmes' own opium use and unorthodox detective methods, a connection creator David Shore built the entire premise around. [The Hollywood Reporter](https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/tv/tv-news/mika-abdalla-stephen-kalyn-dean-allie-off-campus-season-2-1236603976/) Running for eight seasons, the show became the most watched television program in the world in 2008, earning Laurie two Golden Globe Awards and a place in the Guinness Book of World Records, while the Writers Guild of America later ranked it among the 101 best written television series of all time. [ComicBook.com](https://comicbook.com/tv-shows/news/first-look-at-bullseyes-new-costume-revealed-for-daredevil-born-again-season-3-return/) Everybody lies. That single principle carried eight seasons of some of the finest medical television ever produced.
